dea-avc-013.text: The IB team (short consultations) and the IB team ETL (heavy loads) share a cluster Redshift provided and dispute resources in the loading hours. Redshift isolates these loads with priorities and limits?
options: Workload Management (WLM), with separate rows (or Auto) WLM with query priorities) for BI and ETL
Create two users with different passwords
dea-avc-013.explanation: (a) Correct: or WLM sets rows with memory/competition (or Auto priorities) WLM), ensuring that the ETL do not suffocate the BI (and QMR to kill queries out of the pattern).: VACUUM is table maintenance. C) Incorrect: different users do not isolate resources. D) Incorrect: sort keys optimize I/O, do not arbitrate competition between loads..

dea-avc-014.text: The analytics area needs to provide AO data VIVO production warehouse for another cluster Redshift of another business unit, SEM copy data or mount export pipelines. Which resource serves?
options: Redshift Data Sharing: share schemas/tables between clusters (datashare), with live reading and no data movement
dea-avc-014.explanation: A) Incorrect: UNLOAD creates outdated copies and pipeline to maintain. B) Correct: the data sharing exposes objects from a producer cluster to consumers (same account, cross-account or cross-region) with transactionally consistent reading and zero copy. C) Incorrect: DMS between warehouses is gambiarra face. D) Incorrect: weekly snapshots give old data and recurring work.

dea-avc-015.text: Analysts need to cross, in UMA consultation SQL, data from data lake in S3 with a reference table that lives in a RDS PostgreSQL, without replicating the bench to the lake. Athena Allow it.?
options: Athena Federated Query, using a connector (Lambda) for the external source
dea-avc-015.explanation: A) Incorrect: projection resolves partition enumeration. B) Incorrect: CTAS materializes results, does not connect external sources. C) Correct: Federated Query uses connectors based on Lambda to consult external sources (RDS, DynamoDB, Redshift, etc.) and do JOIN with the lake tables in the same consultation. D) Incorrect: workgroups govern use/cost.

dea-avc-016.text: A data lake has IMPRESSIBLE access patterns: some datasets stay stationary for months and are consulted again intensively. SEM risk of recovery rates or latency degradation, and without manually managing transitions. S3 answer?
options: S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which moves objects automatically between layers according to the access pattern
S3 Standard with fixed lifecycle for Glacier in 30 days
dea-avc-016.explanation: A) Correct: Intelligent-Tiering monitors access by object and automatically transitions (frequency-infrequently) without recovery rates in the default layers — made for unpredictable patterns. B) Incorrect: One Zone-IA reduces resilience and collects recovery. C) Incorrect: fixed lifecycle errs when the default is unpredictable (dataset 'cold' can return tomorrow). D) Incorrect: Deep Archive has recovery of hours — unfeasible for sudden return of access.

dea-avc-017.text: The team wants to export the result of queries from Redshift for the curated layer of data lake, in Parquet partitioned, for consumption by Athena What native command does this in parallel and efficient way?
options: UNLOAD ... FORMAT AS PARQUET PARTITION BY, WRITING IN Parallel IN THE S3
dea-avc-017.explanation: A) Incorrect: writing on external tables exists (Spectrum), but the canonical mass export command is the UNLOAD. B) Incorrect: pg_dump does not apply to Redshift to export analytical data to lake. C) Incorrect: COPY It's the way. INVERSO (S3 → Redshift). D) Correct: or UNLOAD record the direct result in S3 in Parquet, with partitioning and parallelism by the slices — the warehouse bridge→lake.

dea-avc-018.text: A table DynamoDB of events has traffic 20x higher on unpredictable promotional dates, suffering throttling in the mode provided even with auto scaling (The priority is to: NUNCA Throttlear, accepting variable cost. Which configuration meets?
options: Capacity mode ON-DEMAND, absorbing sudden peaks without provisioning
dea-avc-018.explanation: A) Incorrect: smaller items help, but do not eliminate the supply gap. B) Incorrect: dimension to 20x normal waste the whole year — and the next peak can be 30(x.C) Incorrect: GSI creates more consumption, no more table capacity. D) Correct: on-demand specifies by request and accommodates instant peaks (including 2x the previous peak immediately) — the trade-off is higher unit cost, accepted by the requirement.

dea-avc-019.text: After weeks of intense loads and exclusions, the consultations of a cluster Redshift provided degraded and storage was not released. Which maintenance operations recover performance and space?
options: VACUUM (rearrange/recover space of leased lines) and ANALYZE (update optimization statistics)
DROP and re-creation of all schemes
dea-avc-019.explanation: A) Correction: VACUUM reorder as the key spell and remove lines marked as deleted; ANALYZE updates the statistics that the planner uses — the classic maintenance double (in large part automatic today, but charged in proof). B) Incorrect: recreate everything is destructive and unnecessary. C) Incorrect: restart does not reorganize data. D) Incorrect: password has no relation to performance.

dea-avc-020.text: A pipeline needs reprocessing 300 historical daily partitions performing the MESMO Job Glue for each partition, with controlled parallelism (max. 10 and tolerance to faults per item. Step Functions implements it elegantly?
options: The state MAP (or Distributed Map for large scale), iterating on the list of partitions with MaxCompetition=10 and Retry/Catch by iteration
A single execution with timeout of 1 year
dea-avc-020.explanation: A) Correct: the Map runs the same sub-machine for each item in the list with limited competition; the Distributed Map scales to millions of items (e.g. objects of the S3) with fault control per item. B) Incorrect: 300 fixed states are impossible to maintain. C) Incorrect: timeout does not create controlled parallelism. D) Incorrect: Wait does not iterate anything.

dea-avc-021.text: A load job is sometimes re-executed after partial failures and started generating REGISTROS DUPLICADOS in the destination. Which principle of pipeline design prevents this and how to apply it?
options: Accept duplicates and treat them on dashboard
Run jobs only once a week
Idepower: re-executions produce the same final state — e.g. overwrite the entire target partition (INSERT OVERWRITE), use MERGE/upsert by key, or deduplication keys
dea-avc-021.explanation: A) Incorrect: push the problem to consumption corrupt metrics and confidence. B) Incorrect: lower frequency does not prevent duplication in re-runs. C) Correct: Idepotent pipeline can be re-executed safely — partition overwrite, MERGE by natural key or dedup by event ID are the standards. D) Incorrect: without hindrances, any transitory failure becomes a manual incident.

dea-avc-022.text: Dashboards shoot at MESMA consultation Athena dozens of times an hour about data that only changes 1x per day, paying full scanning in each execution. Athena Cut this waste without changing the query?
options: Enable Query Result Reuse at an appropriate maximum age, serving the cache result
dea-avc-022.explanation: A) Incorrect: SELECT * Scan MAIS. B) Correct: the result reuse returns the recent result of MESMA consultation without rescanning (you define the maximum acceptable age, ex.: 60 min) — zero scanning cost in repetitions. C) Incorrect: projection optimizes partition enumeration, not repeated queries. D) Incorrect: 'increase workgroup' does not exist as capacity.

dea-avc-023.text: The team wants a unique alert of 'degraded pipeline' that only shoots when (job failure of Glue) And (firehose delivery delay) occur together, avoiding the noise of isolated alarms. CloudWatch implements this logic?
options: Composite Alarm, combining son alarms with logical operators (AND/OR) and a single action
dea-avc-023.explanation: A) Incorrect: two isolated alarms are exactly the noise to avoid. B) Incorrect: log scheduled queries do not replace alarm algebra. C) Correct: the alarm composite evaluates a logical expression on other alarms and only triggers action (SNS/on-call) when the combination is true — reduction of drawing noise. D) Incorrect: dashboard does not notify alone.

dea-avc-024.text: After a bug fixed in the transformation job, it is necessary to REPROCESSAR 90 days of historical data (backfill) without interrupting the daily routine processing. DUAS practices structure this backfill safely? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Run the backfill as a flow SEPARADO and parameterized by date range (ex.: Step Functions Partition map), isolated from the daily pipeline
Pause the daily pipeline by 90 days
Make the backfill partition manually by partition on the console
Delete the lake date and start again
Ensure that the job is matchable by partition (overwrite/merge), so that reruns do not duplicate data
dea-avc-024.explanation: A) Correct: parametrically and parallelized backfill coexists with the diary and is retreadable. B) Incorrect: stop operation because of history is unacceptable. C) Incorrect: 90 manual days = guaranteed human error. D) Incorrect: destroying the lake is disproportionate. E) Correct: partition-based idempotence is what makes reprocessing safe (without duplicates in already corrected windows).
